objects.description: A small value-type type-tagged pointer wrapper that can hold a pointer to any single concrete type and later be queried for that same type; if queried with a different type, get<T>() returns nullptr. It does not own the pointee. Copyable and cheap; no allocations. Type identity is implemented via per-type static address (FastTypeId).

A move-only owning counterpart to AnyPtr. It type-erases ownership of a single heap-allocated object, deleting it with the correct type on destruction via a stored deleter. Constructible from std::unique_ptr<T>. Not copyable; movable. get<T>() returns the stored pointer if T matches the stored type; otherwise nullptr.

Abstract interface for scheduling and executing closures. Implementations must be thread-safe. Provides a virtual destructor and a pure-virtual Schedule method that accepts a std::function<void()> to run.

functions.name: tensorflow::serving::AnyPtr::AnyPtr
functions.description: Default-constructs an AnyPtr representing a null pointer with an internal type tag of void. Use when you need an empty/cleared AnyPtr.
requirements: Constructs a null AnyPtr; no managed lifetime.
Safe to copy and assign; value type.
Pointer is null until constructed from a real pointer.

functions.name: tensorflow::serving::AnyPtr::AnyPtr
functions.description: Constructs an AnyPtr from nullptr, equivalent to the default constructor. Useful for explicit null initialization or resetting.
requirements: Results in a null AnyPtr with type tag void.
No ownership or lifetime management.

functions.name: tensorflow::serving::AnyPtr::get
functions.description: Returns the stored pointer reinterpreted as T* if and only if the AnyPtr was constructed with the exact same type T (including const-qualification); otherwise returns nullptr. Enables type-checked retrieval from a type-erased pointer.
requirements: Must be called with the exact same type T used when constructing the AnyPtr (const and non-const are distinct).
Return may be nullptr either because the stored pointer was null or because T does not match.
Returned pointer is non-owning; caller must not delete it unless they own the object.
Caller must not dereference the returned pointer if it is null.

functions.name: tensorflow::serving::UniqueAnyPtr::UniqueAnyPtr
functions.description: Default-constructs an empty UniqueAnyPtr with no managed object. Behaves like a moved-from or null unique owner.
requirements: Constructs with a null internal pointer and a no-op deleter.
No ownership until constructed from a unique_ptr or moved from another UniqueAnyPtr.

functions.name: tensorflow::serving::UniqueAnyPtr::UniqueAnyPtr
functions.description: Constructs a null UniqueAnyPtr, equivalent to the default constructor.
requirements: Results in an empty UniqueAnyPtr with a no-op deleter.

functions.name: tensorflow::serving::UniqueAnyPtr::UniqueAnyPtr
functions.description: Takes ownership of ptr, erasing its type while retaining a type-specific deleter that will delete the object as T upon destruction. Provides type-checked access via get<T>().
requirements: ptr may be null; if non-null, ownership is transferred and ptr is released (becomes null).
The stored deleter deletes as exactly T; callers must use the same T for get<T>() to retrieve a non-null pointer.
After construction, the original unique_ptr must not be used to delete the object (it has been released).

functions.name: tensorflow::serving::UniqueAnyPtr::~UniqueAnyPtr
functions.description: Destroys the UniqueAnyPtr, invoking its stored deleter on the managed pointer (no-op if null). Ensures owned object is deleted as the recorded type.
requirements: Destructor may be called on empty or non-empty instances.
No action required by caller; ensures single ownership semantics.

functions.name: tensorflow::serving::UniqueAnyPtr::operator=
functions.description: Move-assigns from other by swapping internal pointer and deleter with other. After assignment, this owns other's former object; other becomes the previous state of this.
requirements: Self-move-assignment is safe via swap but typically unnecessary.
After assignment, other is valid but unspecified (effectively the previous state of this).
Copy assignment is deleted; only move assignment is allowed.

functions.name: tensorflow::serving::UniqueAnyPtr::get
functions.description: Returns the stored pointer as T* if the internal type tag matches exactly T (including const-qualification); otherwise returns nullptr. Non-owning view into the owned object.
requirements: Must request the exact same type T that was used to construct the UniqueAnyPtr from std::unique_ptr<T>.
Return may be nullptr if no object is owned or if T does not match.
Returned pointer remains valid while the UniqueAnyPtr remains alive and owning the object; do not delete it manually.

functions.name: tensorflow::serving::UniqueAnyPtr::as_any_ptr
functions.description: Returns a const reference to an AnyPtr view of the stored pointer, enabling type-checked access without transferring ownership.
requirements: The returned AnyPtr reference is valid only as long as the UniqueAnyPtr object remains alive and unchanged.
Do not store the returned reference beyond the lifetime of the UniqueAnyPtr.

functions.name: tensorflow::serving::UniqueAnyPtr::swap
functions.description: Swaps the stored pointer and deleter with other. Useful for implementing move operations and for exception-safe ownership transfers.
requirements: other must be a valid UniqueAnyPtr instance (may be empty).
Safe to call with self, though it is a no-op.

functions.name: tensorflow::serving::Executor::~Executor
functions.description: Virtual default destructor for the Executor interface. Allows proper cleanup via base-class pointers.
requirements: Subclass destructors must be virtual-compatible (inherited from this).
No special caller requirements; invoked automatically when objects are destroyed.

functions.name: tensorflow::serving::Executor::Schedule
functions.description: Schedules the provided callable for execution by the executor. Concrete executors define the execution policy (e.g., thread pool, inline, queued). May block depending on the implementation.
requirements: fn must be a valid callable; it should be safe to invoke with no arguments and must not throw exceptions unless the executor documents handling.
Implementations must be thread-safe; callers may invoke Schedule concurrently.
As a pure virtual function, must be overridden by subclasses.
